newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM says top Khmer Rouge in peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM says top Khmer Rouge in peace talks.

text.p: Nominal Khmer Rouge leader Khieu Samphan has requested a meeting with Cambodian officials to forge an end to the feared rebels' long war with the government, the first prime minister said on Thursday.

"Mr. Khieu Samphan requested us to meet this morning, so the (Cambodian officials) have already gone and this evening when they return, they will report to me," Ranariddh told reporters after attending a school graduation ceremony.
Cambodia PM says top Khmer Rouge in peace talks
Ranariddh would not reveal the location of meeting, only noting it would take place "with support from a country that is friend of Cambodia."

Other top hard-liners, including hated leader Pol Pot - mastermind of the 1975-1979 "killing fields" rule in which more than one million people died - powerful northwest commander Ta Mok and military chief Son Sen, were not participating in the talks, Ranariddh said.
He said Pol Pot may have already left the country but Thai military sources familiar with the issue disputed this.

Ranariddh and co-premier Hun Sen have been at odds over government policy toward the rebels and compete to recruit fighters to their own sides. Since August, thousands of guerrillas have defected to the government and fewer than 2,000 fighters are thought to remain in the last rebel stronghold of Anlong Veng in the north.
